what: Every drive of a game, valued two ways. EPA is what the drive was worth in expected points -- additive down the drive and comparable across games. WPA is what it was worth to winning THIS game, and LEVERAGE is what a touchdown would have been worth from where the drive started. The two disagree often and are meant to: a drive that burns nine minutes while ahead can lose expected points and still gain win probability. Swing plays are the extremes of the drive's own EPA, so a sack, a holding call and a third-down stop all price themselves.
